newsitem.title: LEBANON: Six civilians killed in south Lebanon shelling.
newsitem.headline: Six civilians killed in south Lebanon shelling.

text.p: Israel's local militia allies fired three rounds of shells at Lebanon's southern port city of Sidon on Monday, killing six civilians and wounding 34, many of them seriously, security sources said.

In Jerusalem, an Israeli military source said: "The Israel Defence Forces can say with full assurance it isn't IDF shelling of Sidon," adding that the attack was apparently carried out by forces of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia.
"It is probably a shelling by General (Antoine) Lahd's SLA to avenge the killing of the two youths whose father was a former battalion commander in the SLA," the source said.
The Israeli army said two Lebanese youths were killed and two wounded when an explosive device blew up a vehicle in the Jezzine area of south Lebanon hours before the shelling in Sidon.

In the second round of shelling, two shells hit crowded areas of Sidon and three slammed into the suburbs less than one hour after a shelling attack on the city 40 km (25 miles) south of the capital Beirut.
Victims were taken to five hospitals.
A total of 16 shells landed in Sidon and its suburbs, forcing residents to abandon the city's main road.

Shortly after the shelling subsided, six Katyusha rockets hit Jezzine, an SLA stronghold just north of Israel's south Lebanon security zone, where Israeli forces and pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas often clash.
Hizbollah sources in Beirut said they had no immediate information on the rocket attacks.
Hizbollah's top official in south Lebanon, Nabeel Kawouk, threatened to carry out reprisals for the shelling by pro-Israeli militias.

"We must speak in the language that the Israeli enemy understands and it is not possible to keep silent about ahwat happened today. The enemy must understand a deeply bitter message," he told reporters after visiting some of the wounded in Sidon hospitals.
